solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Temple, a divine one, toured by old man

indicators.note: something toured by another is gone around by it, so the old man's letters surround the divine one

parts.note: PA is an informal word for father, an old man
a god is a divine being

explanation.surface: A father visits a temple dedicated to a god.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered Buddhist or Hindu tower used as a temple in East Asia.

clue.text: A fighter, old ally abroad

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter aircraft

explanation.surface: A fighter plane flown by a long-standing foreign ally.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, so it is an ally in a foreign tongue.

clue.text: Quality of alien with soldiers clutching the head

indicators.note: soldiers clutching something hold it within, so the next word goes inside their letters

parts.note: OR stands for Other Ranks, soldiers who are not officers
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Dungeness

explanation.surface: Something alien about troops grabbing their commanding officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is not a leader but a headland: NESS, as in Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherness is the state of being different or foreign, the essential trait of anything alien.

clue.text: A Welsh girl possibly penning English epic

indicators.note: to pen something is to enclose it, so the girl's name holds the next letter inside

parts.note: Enid is a girl's name of Welsh origin; 'possibly' marks it as one example

explanation.surface: A Welsh girl writing an English epic poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing but means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aeneid is Virgil's Latin epic poem about the wanderings of Aeneas.

clue.text: Fresh sailing just off the south coast of England?

definitions.meaning: fresh in the sense of cheeky or impudent

definitions.text: sailing just off the south coast of England?
definitions.meaning: read as ..., being afloat in the Solent, the strait between the Isle of Wight and Hampshire

explanation.surface: A breezy yachting trip along England's south coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The Solent is the strait separating the Isle of Wight from the English mainland, popular with yachtsmen; the question mark flags the split reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh can mean impertinent or cheeky, which is what an insolent person is.

clue.text: Case: it involves singular person on the fiddle?

parts.note: the instrumental is a grammatical case, found in Russian and other languages

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up or include, so the word it holds the next letter within

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A legal case about someone fiddling the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the fiddle' suggests fraud; here it is someone playing a violin, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrumentalist is a musician who plays an instrument, a violinist being one example.

clue.text: Lazybones fencing yard in daring jumper

indicators.note: fencing something encloses it, so the shirker's letters surround the measure

parts.note: a skiver is a British word for someone who shirks work

explanation.surface: An idler builds a fence round the garden of a bold athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' is not a British sweater but someone who leaps from a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A skydiver leaps from an aircraft and freefalls before opening a parachute, a bold kind of jumping.

clue.text: Fabric a group of stars used to hem cape

indicators.note: a hem encloses an edge, so the constellation's letters go round the cape's abbreviation

parts.note: Lyra, the Lyre, is a constellation
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A starry-patterned material is used to edge a cape.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is the trade name for a stretchy synthetic fibre used in sportswear.

clue.text: State evidence of recent clothes-shopping trip?

definitions.meaning: a ..., a just-bought sweater, shows someone has been shopping for clothes

explanation.surface: Confessing that a new garment proves a shopping spree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jersey' is the British word for a pullover sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: New Jersey is one of the fifty states of the USA, on the east coast.

clue.text: E.g. stealing bit of crockery with a single dirty spot

parts.note: a dish is a piece of crockery
one is a single
a sty, where pigs live, is a filthy place

explanation.surface: Pocketing a piece of crockery from one grubby place.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is an example of dishonesty, acting deceitfully or fraudulently.

clue.text: Hood to intimidate moll, ultimately

parts.note: to cow someone is to intimidate them

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word moll, its final letter

explanation.surface: A gangster sets out to frighten his girlfriend in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hood' and 'moll' paint a gangland scene, but the hood is a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowl is a monk's hood, or a hooded cloak.

clue.text: Attendant's uniform in my bank

indicators.note: one letter sits in another word, so it goes inside the exclamation

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a tier is a row or bank, as of seats

explanation.surface: A servant's livery is kept in the clue-writer's bank.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Attendant' with 's as 'is': an attendant is a courtier.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtier attends a monarch at court, so is a royal attendant.

clue.text: Turkish hostelry welcomed by pilgrim — a retreat

indicators.note: something welcomed by these words is taken in by them, sitting inside the run of letters

explanation.surface: A pilgrim on retreat is welcomed at an inn in Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: An imaret is a Turkish hospice where pilgrims and travellers are lodged.

clue.text: Cheese not lasting long, for the most part

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: brief means short-lived

explanation.surface: A soft cheese that will not keep long.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cow's-milk cheese with a white rind.

clue.text: Minor star playing in very poor conditions

indicators.note: playing suggests acting about, so the letters of these words perform in a new order

explanation.surface: A minor celebrity performing in a dire setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainstorm is heavy rain with wind, meaning very poor weather conditions.

clue.text: King leaves great conductor very regally

indicators.note: when the king leaves, his letter departs from the conductor's title

parts.note: a maestro is a distinguished conductor
R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for king
so means very, as in 'so good'

explanation.surface: A monarch departs while a renowned conductor performs grandly.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestoso is the musical direction to play majestically, in a stately and dignified way.

clue.text: Alternate representation of Turkestan

indicators.note: a representation recasts something in another form, so the letters of the place name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shifting map of a Central Asian region.
explanation.definitionFit: To alternate is to take turns, each doing something in succession.

clue.text: Able to feel bliss, even not very upset

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters are jumbled
not means the letter for very is left out of even

explanation.surface: Someone sensitive enough to be upset even by happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not very' drops V from EVEN, leaving EEN; with BLISS these letters are jumbled ('upset').
explanation.definitionFit: Sensible in its older meaning is perceptible or capable of sensation, as in 'sensible of the cold'.

clue.text: German's a mug or a genius

parts.note: ein is German for a
a stein is a German beer mug

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a German man is a fool or brilliant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mug' looks like a fool, opposite of genius, but it is the beer mug.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein's name is used for any genius, as in 'he's no Einstein'.

clue.text: Decisive blow spinning ruminant round

indicators.note: spinning turns the animal around, so its letters are read backwards

parts.note: a yak is a cud-chewing ox
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A knockout punch sends a yak spinning round.
explanation.definitionFit: Kayo is a spelling of KO, a knockout, the blow that ends a boxing match.

clue.text: Routine drug overdose

parts.note: meth is short for methamphetamine

explanation.surface: A habitual drug user overdoses.
explanation.definitionFit: A method is an established procedure, a routine way of doing something.

clue.text: Part of hands holding small book

indicators.note: hands holding something grasp it, so the palms' letters enclose the next one

parts.note: palms are the inner surfaces of the hands

explanation.surface: Hands clasping a little book.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalms is a book of the Old Testament, a collection of sacred songs.

clue.text: Renaissance painter is cheeky in speech

indicators.note: in speech signals the word is spoken, sounding like the painter's name

parts.note: lippy is British slang for impertinent, cheeky

explanation.surface: An insolent Italian master with a sharp tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Filippo Lippi and his son Filippino were Florentine painters of the fifteenth century.

clue.text: Blue put on a green space, which is random

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece put on another is added after it, so the blue comes last

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or grassy field
blue is the colour of the Conservatives, so a Tory is a blue

explanation.surface: Something blue placed on a lawn at random.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' is not sad or a colour here but a Conservative, as in British politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleatory means depending on chance, so it describes anything random.

clue.text: Hastened, say, to return in Sierra?

parts.note: ran means hastened

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: e.g., for example, is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: Rushing back to the Sierra mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sierra' is a mountain range; the question mark warns it is not the NATO letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a long jagged chain of mountains, so it is an example of a range.

clue.text: Person returned to office after business school

indicators.note: after places the MP behind the business abbreviation

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
an MP, Member of Parliament, is returned to office at an election

explanation.surface: Someone heading back to work after studying at business school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'business school' looks like one phrase, but 'school' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Comp is British slang for a comprehensive, a state secondary school taking all abilities.

clue.text: Backing one-pound operas is foolish

indicators.note: backing runs things in reverse, so the one and pound are read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
LB is the abbreviation for a pound weight
The Ring is Wagner's cycle of four operas

explanation.surface: Betting a single pound on opera is idiotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' suggests betting, but here it turns I and LB round to BLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithering means utterly foolish, as in 'blithering idiot'.

clue.text: Two versions of this person's books about to arrive

parts.note: this person's can be read as I'M (this person is) and as MINE (belonging to this person)
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: The writer has two editions of their own books on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this person' is the setter speaking; 's is read once as 'is' and once as possession.
explanation.definitionFit: Imminent means about to happen, close at hand.

clue.text: One on the pull at Christmas — the Queen?

definitions.text: One on the pull at Christmas — the Queen?

parts.words: One on the pull at Christmas — the Queen?
parts.note: a reindeer pulling Santa's sleigh, whose name ends with the Queen's letters ER

explanation.walkthrough: The Queen is ER in crossword convention, which ends the name; 'on the pull' is British slang for seeking a date.
explanation.definitionFit: Dasher is one of Santa's reindeer that pull his sleigh on Christmas Eve.
